key_evidence_accepted: The Supreme Court accepted the affidavit filed by the victims stating that the disputes between the parties were settled and they expressed their willingness to compound the offence.
trial_duration: Offence on 23.7.1986; trial judgment dated April 30, 1994; High Court judgment dated 14.9.2006 and 9.11.2006; Supreme Court decision on April 9, 2010
legal_representation: Meenakshi Arora for the Appellant; Hemantika Wahi, Shamik Sanjanwala, Jesal, Anurag Sharma for the Respondents
investigation_status: Trial completed; charge sheet filed; FIR registered
appeal_history: Trial court: Conviction and sentence affirmed; High Court: Permission to compound offence rejected; Supreme Court: Appeal allowed, judgments set aside, permission to compound granted
prosecution_argument: The State argued that the offence under Section 324 IPC, which became non-compoundable under the Code of Criminal Procedure (Amendment) Act, 2005, should not be compounded.
defence_argument: The defence argued that the offence was committed before the amendment came into force and thus was compoundable with the permission of the Court.
legal_principle_applied: The Court applied the principle that the Code of Criminal Procedure (Amendment) Act, 2005 is not applicable to offences committed before its commencement.
other_sentence_order: The Court permitted the victims to compound the offence punishable under Section 324 IPC, which resulted in the acquittal of the accused under Section 320(8) of the Code of Criminal Procedure.
